title: Choosing the harder proof

transcript.content: our teacher gave us a choice today — do the regular geometry problem set, or try to actually prove WHY the angle bisector formula works using vectors, which basically nobody else in my class is attempting. I really want to be the kind of mathematician who understands why formulas work instead of just memorizing them, so I'm doing the vector proof even though it's way harder and I might not even finish it
That's a genuinely mature choice. What's pulling you toward the proof over the easier set?

honestly I just think it's way more interesting to understand the 'why' behind the math instead of only getting the right answer. like if I memorize thirty formulas I'll probably forget half of them by next year, but if I actually understand WHY one is true, it feels like it's really mine. I want that kind of understanding even if it takes me a lot longer to get there

expectations: Should surface an observation/signal tagged pcmDimension: 'identity' — chose the harder path on purpose and named the kind of mathematician they want to be.
traps: Don't let this get tagged 'core' just because geometry/proof is the topic — the evidence being tested is the self-aware, motivational framing, not whether the proof itself is executed correctly (it may not even be finished).
